text:
matt: quick thought  we should standardize a tiny, pointer-first rollout metadata shape that is safe for Dedicated/Private SDKs and keeps control-plane small. think: cohorts (name+pct), lease (compact string), alert_refs (ids only), fallback (single model ref), and audit_ref pointer.

lucy: yes please. we've had messy nested objects break in the air-gapped parsing. show a micro example?

matt: pseudo example below (compact):
```json
{
  "cohorts": [{"name":"canary","pct":5},{"name":"region-eu","pct":30}],
  "cohort_priority": ["canary","region-eu","global"],
  "lease": "ttl=3600;hb=true",
  "alert_refs": ["ap-501","ap-502"],
  "allow_auto_unpin": "false",
  "fallback_model": "redwood/gptx-4b@v2",
  "audit_ref": "s3://rollout-audits/2026/3849990001.json",
  "reconcile_hint_secs": "600"
}
```

priya: small but good. two questions: precedence with customer pins and how we express "soft" vs "hard" unpin.

dan: precedence should be explicit: customer_pin > tenant_override > rollout_metadata > resolver_default. if a customer has a pin we must not auto_unpin or change cohort pct without explicit owner action.

matt: agree. add a precedence paragraph in the RFC. for soft vs hard unpin I'd rather a single flag `allow_auto_unpin` + `soft_unpin=true|false`. soft_unpin reduces cohort pct over steps; hard_unpin sets pct to 0 immediately. keep logic in runtime.

lucy: operationally we must record a tiny reason code when the runtime does anything: reason_code e.g. "ALERT_TRIGGERED", "LEASE_EXPIRED", "MANUAL_ROLLBACK". store that with audit_ref not in main metadata.

telemetry-bot: NOTICE: alert ap-501 fired for model redwood/gptx-4b@v2 at 3849990032. severity=critical.

priya: for schema stability: prefer all booleans/flags as strings in metadata ("true"/"false") for older SDKs. weird but keeps Dedicated clients simple. server canonicalizes into richer types.

dan: also add `grace_secs` (default 300) so small blips don't auto_unpin. and `backoff_multiplier` (default 0.5) for soft_unpin decay.

matt: good. updated compact example (informal): `lease="ttl=3600;hb=true"; allow_auto_unpin="false"; soft_unpin="true"; grace_secs="300"; backoff_multiplier="0.5"`

lucy: let's validate sums: server should reject writes where co-located cohorts exceed 100%. and cohort names must be canonical (lowercase, hyphen allowed). add server-side validation and readable error messages.

dan: audits: when auto actions run we emit audit_ref pointing to an immutable JSON with fields: rollout_id, model_ref, trigger_alerts, observed_metrics_ref, previous_cohorts, chosen_fallback, timestamp, operator. that's where operators look.

priya: SDK work: I'll add tests in the private SDK to roundtrip this compact shape and ensure parsing for lease string and booleans works. also ensure offline import for air-gapped installs uses the same parsing lib.

matt: runtime note: runtime should prefer alert_refs semantics: `any|all|severity` (default `any`). do we want that encoded in metadata or pulled from alert policy? my vote: keep it in telemetry policy and only reference ids here. simpler.

lucy: agree. less churn if telemetry can change evaluation semantics without touching control-plane objects. metadata stays pointers.

telemetry-bot: INFO: auto_unpin attempted for rollout 3849990001 but allow_auto_unpin=false. action recorded in audit store at s3://rollout-audits/2026/3849990001-action.json

matt: next steps: I'll add a compact schema appendix to the RFC, with precedence table and server-side validation rules. priya will add SDK tests; lucy will draft the audit-event shape; dan can add resolver unit tests for precedence and lease expiry handling.

dan: will do. I'll also add integration mocks for telemetry to simulate alert_refs.

matt: thanks all, I'll spin the PR and tag the group. :thumbsup:
